speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any other symptoms like double vision, difficulty swallowing, or weakness in your arms and legs?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Vitamin B12 and Erythrocyte Folate Levels.
REQUEST TEST: Serum Copper and Ceruloplasmin.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
While I note the previous suggestion of Multiple Sclerosis, the specific combination of gait and limb ataxia with your medical history raises concern for other conditions like Spinocerebellar Ataxias or Wilson's disease. Have you or your family experienced any tremors, slurred speech, or changes in personality or behavior?

REQUEST TEST: Serum Copper, Ceruloplasmin, and Alpha-1 Antitrypsin levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with focus on cerebellum and brainstem.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent lab results showing normal readings for blood counts, metabolic panels, vitamins, and copper/ceruloplasmin help rule out metabolic deficiencies and Wilson's disease. Given the persistence of your ataxia and the previous mention of Multiple Sclerosis, could you clarify if you have noticed any specific sensory changes like numbness, tingling, or a "pins and needles" sensation in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the metabolic and copper studies were normal, and you have ataxia without significant sensory deficits, does your previous neurologist mention any family members with similar walking or coordination problems?

REQUEST TEST: Genetic testing panel for Spinocerebellar Ataxias (SCA1, SCA2, SCA3, SCA6).
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with focus on cerebellum and brainstem.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Genetic testing panel for Spinocerebellar Ataxias (SCA1, SCA2, SCA3, SCA6): NORMAL READINGS; MRI Brain with focus on cerebellum and brainstem: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are highly specific for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Given your history of gait and limb ataxia, have you been diagnosed with HIV/AIDS or currently taking immunosuppressive medications for another condition?

REQUEST TEST: HIV Antigen/Antibody Combo Test, CD4 Count, and Immunosuppressive Medication Review.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV Antigen/Antibody Combo Test: Positive; CD4 Count: 45 cells/µL; Immunosuppressive Medication Review: Confirmed use of natalizumab for Crohn disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to AIDS and immunosuppressive therapy with natalizumab.
